name: Atrioventricular Valve Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Atrioventricular Valve Anomalies

criteria.description: Abnormal morphology of the atrioventricular valve leaflets detected by echocardiography
Presence of atrioventricular valve regurgitation confirmed by Doppler imaging
Identification of associated cardiac malformations such as atrial or ventricular septal defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal valve morphology and evidence of valve regurgitation on echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging findings; genetic testing may support but is not diagnostic.

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Possible anemia secondary to chronic illness
imaging: Echocardiography showing valve leaflet malformation and regurgitation
Cardiac MRI for detailed valve anatomy and function
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with congenital heart defects (e.g., NKX2-5, GATA4) may be present
other: Electrocardiogram showing atrial enlargement or arrhythmias
Cardiac catheterization for hemodynamic assessment in complex cases

distinguishingFeatures: Valve leaflet thickening and prolapse without congenital malformation
Less commonly associated with septal defects
Isolated tricuspid valve malformation often with Ebstein anomaly features
Characteristic apical displacement of septal leaflet

redFlags: Severe valve regurgitation causing refractory heart failure
Sudden onset of arrhythmias or syncope
